title: O'Brien's Test
text: O’Brien’s OLS statistic sum t-statistics obtained standardizing individual endpoints pooled within-group sample standard deviations. GLS statistic weighted version OLS.

title: O'Brien's Test
text: provide obrien() function conduct O’Brien’s statistical test multiple endpoints across two (treatment) groups. input dataset treatment column one additional column outcome (.e., wide-format). examples use mtept dataset included multcomp package. One important point O’Brien’s test directional nature. Therefore, important adjust outcome metrics similar directions indicate similar outcomes – e.g., positive effect E4 negative effect E1 indicate positive outcome patient, signs reversed align positive outcomes across endpoints. words, endpoints either positively negatively correlated (). data, can see E1, E2, E3 positively correlated. However, E4 negatively correlated endpoints. Therefore, need reverse direction E4 testing.
code: library(gst) library(dplyr) #>  #> Attaching package: 'dplyr' #> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats': #>  #>     filter, lag #> The following objects are masked from 'package:base': #>  #>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union  # load data from the `multcomp` package dat <- multcomp::mtept head(dat) #>    treatment E1 E2 E3 E4 #> 1    Placebo  4  3  3  5 #> 5    Placebo  5  0  1  7 #> 9    Placebo  1  0  1  9 #> 13   Placebo  4  0  3  5 #> 17   Placebo  3  0  2  9 #> 21   Placebo  4  1  2  6 # correlation between endpoints dat |>    select(-treatment) |>    cor() #>            E1         E2         E3         E4 #> E1  1.0000000  0.4166472  0.6437159 -0.7112218 #> E2  0.4166472  1.0000000  0.4605603 -0.4555092 #> E3  0.6437159  0.4605603  1.0000000 -0.6391847 #> E4 -0.7112218 -0.4555092 -0.6391847  1.0000000 # reverse E4 dat <- dat |>   mutate(     E4 = -E4   )  # correlation between endpoints dat |>    select(-treatment) |>    cor() #>           E1        E2        E3        E4 #> E1 1.0000000 0.4166472 0.6437159 0.7112218 #> E2 0.4166472 1.0000000 0.4605603 0.4555092 #> E3 0.6437159 0.4605603 1.0000000 0.6391847 #> E4 0.7112218 0.4555092 0.6391847 1.0000000

title: O'Brien's Test
text: example, let’s perform O’Brien’s test using OLS method equal variances (default).
code: results <- dat |>   obrien(     endpoint_vars = c("E1", "E2", "E3", "E4"),     treatment_vars = "treatment",     method = "ols"   ) print(data.frame(results[-5])) #>   statistic  df      pvalue alternative #> t -2.697624 109 0.008094326   two.sided

title: O'Brien's Test
code: results <- dat |>   obrien(     endpoint_vars = c("E1", "E2", "E3", "E4"),     treatment_vars = "treatment",     method = "gls"   ) print(data.frame(results[-5])) #>   statistic  df      pvalue alternative #> t -2.812559 109 0.005830776   two.sided

title: O'Brien's Test
code: results <- dat |>   obrien(     endpoint_vars = c("E1", "E2", "E3", "E4"),     treatment_vars = "treatment",     method = "ranksum"    ) print(data.frame(results[-5])) #>   statistic  df     pvalue alternative #> t -2.084701 109 0.03943257   two.sided

title: O'Brien's Test
text: example, perform OLS equal variances method possible combinations 4 endpoints.
code: # generate all possible combinations of the 4 endpoints (1 = include; 0 = exclude) opt_mat <- expand.grid(0:1, 0:1, 0:1, 0:1) opt_mat <- opt_mat |> dplyr::arrange(rowSums(opt_mat)) endpoints <- c("E1", "E2", "E3", "E4")  # run o'brien's test on each combination of endpoints results <-    purrr::map_dfr(     2:nrow(opt_mat),     function(i) {       my_endpoints <- endpoints[ opt_mat[i, ] == 1 ]  # identify endpoints to test       x <- dat |>         obrien(           endpoint_vars = my_endpoints,           treatment_vars = "treatment",           method = "ols"          )       x$R <- NULL    # ignore correlation matrix in output (not needed)       x |>         dplyr::as_tibble() |>         dplyr::mutate(           endpoints = paste(my_endpoints, collapse = ", "),           method = "ols"         )     }   )  # display results in a nice table results |>   dplyr::transmute(     Endpoints = endpoints,     DF = df,     `Test Statistic` = round(statistic, 2),     `P-value` = round(pvalue, 3)   ) |>   gt::gt() |>   gt::fmt_auto() |>   gt::tab_header(     "O'Brien's OLS Test on All Endpoint Combinations"   )

title: O'Brien's Test
text: Example 4 provides nice illustration including additional endpoints impact global statistical test (GST). particular, E3 significant (α=0.05\alpha = 0.05) ’s , significant considered jointly endpoint. Another observation reversed direction E4, seen non-significant result combination {E1, E4} despite significant individually jointly reversing E4.

text: Initial release. Includes functions launch two shiny applications: GST Power App: gst_power_app() Make Forestplot App: make_forestplot_app() GST Power App can used run power sample size calculations Global Statistical Test variety scenarios. Additional details can found vignette. Make Forestplot App allows users easily generate forestplot uploading data, copy/pasting spreadsheet, manually typing. resulting plot can resized visually customized variety ways. Also included options handle endpoints inverted directionality different scales. See vignette additional details.
